title: The Strange Story of Punch and Judy
speaker: Alastair Budge

sentences.en: Hello, hello, hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English, the show where you can listen to fascinating stories and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎收听由 Leonardo English 制作的《English Learning for Curious Minds》，这是一个你可以收听精彩故事、了解世界上光怪陆离的事物，同时还能提高英语水平的节目。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today it's the start of another three-part mini-series, this time on unusual British traditions.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，今天我们开始另一个三集迷你系列的节目，这次的主题是不寻常的英国传统。

sentences.en: In today's episode, part one, we are going to be talking about Punch and Judy, the strange, violent, and originally Italian puppet show that became one of Britain’s best-known seaside traditions.
sentences.zh: 在今天的节目（第一部分）中，我们将聊聊 Punch and Judy，这个奇怪、暴力、最初源自意大利的木偶戏，后来成了英国最著名的海滨传统之一。

sentences.en: In part two, we turn to fox hunting, a very different type of tradition that is technically illegal, but still goes on up and down the country.
sentences.zh: 在第二部分中，我们将转向猎狐，这是一种截然不同的传统，按技术上来说是违法的，但在全国上下依然在上演。

sentences.en: And in part three, we are going to be talking about the rise and fall of the British seaside holiday.
sentences.zh: 而在第三部分中，我们将聊聊英国海滨度假的兴衰。

sentences.en: OK then, let's not waste a minute and get right into it.
sentences.zh: 好了，那我们一分钟也不要浪费，直接切入正题吧。

sentences.en: Let me start this episode by teaching you a completely pointless piece of English vocabulary.
sentences.zh: 先让我用一个完全无用的英语词汇来开启这期节目。

sentences.en: It's a word I almost guarantee you've never heard, and that applies even if you are a native speaker.
sentences.zh: 这是一个我敢保证你从未听过的词，即便你是母语者也不例外。

sentences.en: That word is a swazzle. S-W-A-Z-Z-L-E. It's a small metal device you can put in your mouth that turns your voice into something so unusual I don't think I'm even going to try to describe it.
sentences.zh: 这个词就是 swazzle（发音为 S-W-A-Z-Z-L-E）。这是一个可以放进嘴里的小金属装置，能把你的声音变得极其古怪，我想我甚至都不会去尝试描述它。

sentences.en: I'll just play it for you:
sentences.zh: 我直接放给你们听：

sentences.en: That is the voice of a character called Mr Punch, the star of the strange British tradition of the Punch and Judy show.
sentences.zh: 这就是那个叫 Mr Punch 的角色的声音，他是英国奇异传统 Punch and Judy 木偶戏的主角。

sentences.en: Now, Punch and Judy is one of those things that feels deeply, perhaps even quintessentially, British.
sentences.zh: 如今，Punch and Judy 让人感觉是那种深入骨髓、甚至可以说是最典型的英国特色。

sentences.en: A small red-and-white striped booth on a beach.
sentences.zh: 海滩上一个红白相间的简易小帐篷。

sentences.en: A hook-nosed puppet with a squeaky voice, a stick in his hand, and a crowd of children laughing along.
sentences.zh: 一个鹰钩鼻、捏着尖细嗓音的木偶，手里拿着一根棍子，引得周围一群孩子哈哈大笑。

sentences.en: It feels about as British as fish and chips, wet deckchairs and disappointing summer weather.
sentences.zh: 这感觉就像炸鱼薯条、湿漉漉的沙滩椅和令人失望的夏天天气一样充满英国味。

sentences.en: It is also, in its origins, not really British at all; it's Italian.
sentences.zh: 然而从它的起源来看，它其实一点也不英国，它是意大利的。

sentences.en: So, let's start with where it comes from, and how it got to Britain.
sentences.zh: 所以，让我们从它的出处以及它是如何来到英国的开始讲起。

sentences.en: In the early seventeenth century, in the streets and squares of Naples, something called commedia dell'arte was flourishing.
sentences.zh: 十七世纪初，在那不勒斯的街道和小广场上，一种名为“即兴喜剧”（commedia dell'arte）的艺术形式正在蓬勃发展。

sentences.en: Now, commedia dell'arte was a kind of improvised street comedy, performed by travelling players who would arrive in a town, set up a stage, and entertain crowds with rude jokes, slapstick music, and stock characters that everyone in the audience already knew.
sentences.zh: 当时，即兴喜剧是一种街头滑稽戏，由四处巡演的演员表演。他们来到一个城镇，搭起一个舞台，用粗俗的笑话、滑稽的动作以及观众们都耳熟能详的脸谱化角色来取悦大众。

sentences.en: One of those stock characters was a man called Pulcinella.
sentences.zh: 其中一个脸谱化角色名叫 Pulcinella。

sentences.en: He was a Neapolitan invention, and he had a hooked nose and a hump on his back.
sentences.zh: 他是那不勒斯人的创造，有着鹰钩鼻和驼背。

sentences.en: He wore a white costume, a black mask, and he spoke in a strange, squawking voice, a bit like the one you heard a minute ago.
sentences.zh: 他穿着白色戏服，戴着黑色面具，说话声音怪异而刺耳，有点像你们刚才听到的那样。

sentences.en: He wasn't a nice man. He was cunning, lazy, greedy, and easily upset.
sentences.zh: 他不是个好人。他狡猾、懒惰、贪婪，而且很容易暴躁。

sentences.en: He hit people. He insulted figures of authority.
sentences.zh: 他打人。他侮辱权威人士。

sentences.en: He was the sort of character someone in seventeenth-century Naples wasn't meant to admire, but would laugh at anyway.
sentences.zh: 他正是那种十七世纪那不勒斯人不该去崇拜，但又会忍不住嘲笑的角色。

sentences.en: The name Pulcinella is thought to have come from the Italian word "pulcino", which means "little chick", baby chicken, so it's a reference to his beaky, chicken-like face and funny, almost bird-like voice.
sentences.zh: 人们认为 Pulcinella 这个名字源自意大利语“pulcino”，意思是“小鸡”或刚孵化的小鸡，因此这是在暗指他那像鸟喙一样尖的脸和滑稽的、几乎像鸟叫一样的声音。

sentences.en: Now, Pulcinella was a hit in 17th century Naples.
sentences.zh: 在 17 世纪的那不勒斯，Pulcinella 大受欢迎。

sentences.en: And like all hits, he travelled. Italian performers took him to Paris, where he became Polichinelle.
sentences.zh: 和所有热门事物一样，他开始四处旅行。意大利演员把他带到了巴黎，在那里他成了 Polichinelle。

sentences.en: They took him to other European cities, where his name was tweaked or translated.
sentences.zh: 他们又把他带到其他欧洲城市，他的名字也随之被微调或翻译。

sentences.en: And on the 9th of May 1662, he came to London.
sentences.zh: 1662 年 5 月 9 日，他来到了伦敦。

sentences.en: We know that date because of a man called Samuel Pepys.
sentences.zh: 我们之所以知道这个日期，是因为一个叫 Samuel Pepys 的人。

sentences.en: Pepys is one of the most useful figures in English history.
sentences.zh: Pepys 是英国历史上最重要的人物之一。

sentences.en: For nearly a decade he kept a detailed personal diary that recorded everything he ate, drank, gossiped about, and went to see.
sentences.zh: 近十年来，他坚持写详细的个人日记，记录了他吃过的每一顿饭、喝过的每一杯酒、听到过的每一桩八卦以及看过的每一场演出。

sentences.en: And an extra little fun fact about Samuel Pepys is that he wrote one of the most detailed accounts of the Great Fire of London, which happened in 1666, and as the flames approached his house, he dug a big hole to protect his most prized possessions, the first of which was his parmesan cheese.
sentences.zh: 关于 Samuel Pepys 还有一个有趣的冷知识，那就是他写下了关于 1666 年伦敦大火最详尽的记录之一。当大火逼近他的房子时，他挖了一个大坑来保护他最珍贵的财产，而排在第一位的竟然是他的帕玛森奶酪。

sentences.en: And as one more side note, we do have an episode on The Great Fire of London.
sentences.zh: 顺便提一下，我们其实有一期关于伦敦大火的节目。

sentences.en: It's one of our member-only ones, and it's episode number 115.
sentences.zh: 那是我们的会员专享节目之一，即第 115 期。

sentences.en: Anyway, back to the story. On that particular Friday in May 1662, Samuel Pepys walked through Covent Garden in central London and stopped to watch a puppet show.
sentences.zh: 言归正传。在 1662 年 5 月那个特定的星期五，Samuel Pepys 穿过伦敦市中心的考芬园（Covent Garden），停下来观看了一场木偶戏。

sentences.en: The puppeteer was an Italian known as Signor Bologna.
sentences.zh: 木偶操纵者是一位名叫 Signor Bologna 的意大利人。

sentences.en: He was performing a marionette show, which is a show with stringed puppets, and one of his characters was a hook-nosed troublemaker called Punchinello, the Anglicised version of Pulcinella.
sentences.zh: 他表演的是一场提线木偶戏（marionette show），也就是用细绳操纵的木偶戏，其中一个角色是一个鹰钩鼻的捣蛋鬼 Punchinello，也就是 Pulcinella 的英语化版本。

sentences.en: Pepys was impressed. He described the show as "very pretty, the best that ever I saw, and a great resort of gallants."
sentences.zh: Pepys 印象深刻。他将这场演出形容为“非常精彩，是我见过最好的，而且吸引了大量时髦的上流社会人士汇聚于此。”

sentences.en: A great resort of gallants is an unusual phrase, and not something you'd hear nowadays, but it just means a fashionable crowd.
sentences.zh: “大量时髦的上流社会人士”（A great resort of gallants）是一个不寻常的短语，现在已经听不到了，但它其实就是指时髦的人群。

sentences.en: In other words, it was a show for adults, not children.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这是一场给成年人看的演出，而不是给小孩子看的。

sentences.en: Within months, Pepys had seen the show again.
sentences.zh: 几个月后，Pepys 又看了一次这场演出。

sentences.en: And he was not the only fan. Later that same year, King Charles II, the recently restored king of England, asked Signor Bologna to perform for him at his palace.
sentences.zh: 而且他并不是唯一的粉丝。同年晚些时候，刚复辟不久的英国国王查理二世（King Charles II）邀请 Signor Bologna 在他的宫殿里为他进行表演。

sentences.en: The king was so delighted that he gave the puppeteer a gold chain and medal worth twenty-five pounds, which works out at something like five thousand Euros in today's money.
sentences.zh: 国王非常高兴，赏赐给这位木偶艺人一条价值二十五英镑的金链和奖章，折合现在的货币大约相当于五千欧元。

sentences.en: That date, the 9th of May 1662, is now traditionally treated as Mr Punch's UK birthday.
sentences.zh: 1662 年 5 月 9 日这一天，现在传统上被视为 Mr Punch 的英国生日。

sentences.en: There is even a small festival held in Covent Garden each May to mark it.
sentences.zh: 每年五月，考芬园甚至还会举办一个小型的节日来庆祝它。

sentences.en: But the character that Pepys saw that afternoon was still, in every meaningful sense, an Italian visitor.
sentences.zh: 但 Pepys 那天下午看到的那个角色，在任何有意义的层面上，依然是一个来自意大利的访客。

sentences.en: The journey from Italian puppet to British icon would take the best part of two centuries.
sentences.zh: 从一个意大利木偶演变成英国的文化标志，花了将近两个世纪的时间。

sentences.en: The first thing that needed to change was the puppet itself.
sentences.zh: 首先需要改变的是木偶本身。

sentences.en: The original Mr Punch, Pulcinella, was a marionette: a puppet on strings, operated from above.
sentences.zh: 最初的 Mr Punch，即 Pulcinella，是一个提线木偶（marionette）：一种用绳子从上方操纵的木偶。

sentences.en: Putting on a marionette show requires a large stage and quite a lot of kit.
sentences.zh: 上演一场提线木偶戏需要一个大舞台和相当多的装备。

sentences.en: A glove puppet, on the other hand, sits directly on the performer's hand.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，手套木偶（glove puppet）直接套在表演者的手上。

sentences.en: The puppeteer stands hidden inside a simple vertical fabric booth, holds his hands above his head, and operates the puppets from below.
sentences.zh: 木偶师藏在一个简单的垂直布罩里面，把双手举过头顶，从下方操纵木偶。

sentences.en: The booth can be a single striped canvas sheet thrown over a frame.
sentences.zh: 这个布罩可以只是一张套在框架上的红白条纹帆布。

sentences.en: The whole thing is very light, and can be set up and packed away in a matter of minutes.
sentences.zh: 整个东西非常轻便，几分钟内就能搭好并收拾妥当。

sentences.en: Whatsmore, glove puppets move in a completely different way to marionettes.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，手套木偶的运动方式与提线木偶完全不同。

sentences.en: Marionettes move gracefully, slowly, like they're floating in the air.
sentences.zh: 提线木偶动作优雅、缓慢，就像漂浮在空中一样。

sentences.en: Glove puppets are different. Everything is more physical.
sentences.zh: 手套木偶则不同。一切都更加充满肢体动作。

sentences.en: You can throw them around. You can have one whack another over the head with a thud.
sentences.zh: 你可以把它们扔来扔去。你可以用一声闷响，让一个木偶猛击另一个木偶的头部。

sentences.en: You can throw a baby out of a window. You can fight a crocodile, slapping it with a stick.
sentences.zh: 你可以把一个小婴儿扔出窗外。你可以与鳄鱼搏击，用棍子抽打它。

sentences.en: In fact, the word " slapstick " comes from this world, as in " slapstick comedy", the style of exaggerated comedy where people bang into walls or pretend to hurt themselves.
sentences.zh: 事实上，“slapstick”（滑稽闹剧）这个词就源于这个世界，正如“slapstick comedy”（打闹喜剧）那样，这是一种夸张的喜剧风格，人们会撞到墙上或假装伤害自己。

sentences.en: So at some point in the eighteenth century, Punch made the leap from one form to the other, from marionette to glove puppet.
sentences.zh: 所以在十八世纪的某个时候，Punch 完成了从一种形式到另一种形式的跨越，从提线木偶变成了手套木偶。

sentences.en: And this is when things really started to take off.
sentences.zh: 而正是在这个时候，事情真正开始腾飞了。

sentences.en: A glove puppet show could be set up at the corner of a busy street, performed for an hour, and packed away in a wheelbarrow.
sentences.zh: 手套木偶戏可以搭在繁华街角，表演一个小时，然后收进独轮车里。

sentences.en: The whole thing was portable, cheap, and perfectly suited to street performance.
sentences.zh: 整个装置便携、便宜，非常适合街头表演。

sentences.en: This new kind of show needed a new kind of performer.
sentences.zh: 这种新类型的演出需要一种新类型的表演者。

sentences.en: And it could all be operated by one person, who would stand inside the booth and operate the puppets with both hands.
sentences.zh: 而且这一切都可以由一个人完成，他站在布罩内，用双手操纵木偶。

sentences.en: He became known as a " professor ". Why " professor ", nobody is quite sure.
sentences.zh: 他被称为“教授”（professor）。为什么叫“教授”，谁也说不准。

sentences.en: It seems to have been a slightly grand, slightly playful title, given to a man who had mastered a craft that was difficult and not entirely respectable.
sentences.zh: 这似乎是一个稍微有点夸张、稍微有点诙谐的头衔，赋予了一个精通某种既困难又并非完全体面的手艺的人。

sentences.en: The professor also had a secret weapon, and it was the same secret weapon that Italian Pulcinella had used a century before.
sentences.zh: 这位“教授”还有一个秘密武器，正是当年意大利的 Pulcinella 在一个世纪前使用过的那个秘密武器。

sentences.en: A small metal reed, held against the roof of the mouth, that gave Punch his unmistakable, ear-piercing, squeaky voice.
sentences.zh: 一个小小的金属簧片，顶在上颚，赋予了 Punch 那标志性的、刺耳的尖锐嗓音。

sentences.en: In English, this device became known, as you now know, as a swazzle.
sentences.zh: 在英语中，这个装置正如你们现在所知，被称为 swazzle。

sentences.en: Now, I have to confess that I have never tried it, but it does appear that the swazzle is not an easy piece of kit to use.
sentences.zh: 现在，我必须承认我从未尝试过，但看起来 swazzle 确实不是一个好驾驭的装备。

sentences.en: You need to shape the words clearly while forcing air through the reed, switching between Punch’s voice and your normal voice, all while making sure you don’t accidentally swallow the thing.
sentences.zh: 你需要在通过簧片强行吹气的同时清晰地吐字，在 Punch 的声音和你的正常声音之间切换，同时还得确保自己不会不小心把它吞下去。

sentences.en: But if you manage it, if you master it, you'll be able to produce something that sounds like a chicken arguing through a child's toy whistle.
sentences.zh: 但如果你成功了，如果你掌握了它，你就能发出一种听起来像是一只鸡通过儿童玩具哨子在吵架的声音。

sentences.en: Punch professors trained for years to use one properly, and even today the swazzle is considered the badge of a real Punch and Judy performer.
sentences.zh: Punch 教授们要训练多年才能熟练使用它，即使在今天，swazzle 也被视为真正的 Punch and Judy 表演者的徽章。

sentences.en: If you cannot do the voice, you are not accepted as a real Punch man.
sentences.zh: 如果你发不出这种声音，你就不会被认可为真正的 Punch 艺人。

sentences.en: Punch also got a new wardrobe. The plain white Italian costume was dropped, and by the middle of the eighteenth century Punch had taken on the red and yellow colours of the English jester, with a tall pointy hat and a stick in his hand.
sentences.zh: Punch 还换了新行头。朴素的白色意大利戏服被抛弃了，到了十八世纪中叶，Punch 穿上了英国弄臣的红黄两色服装，戴着一顶高高的尖顶帽，手里拿着一根棍子。

sentences.en: He looked, in other words, less like a Neapolitan street performer and more like a figure from a medieval English court.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他看起来不那么像一个那不勒斯街头艺人，而更像是一个中世纪英国宫廷里的人物。

sentences.en: He also gained a cast, supporting actors, or rather, supporting puppets.
sentences.zh: 他还获得了一个演员阵容，也就是配角，或者更准确地说是配角木偶。

sentences.en: And this is where the story gets a bit complicated.
sentences.zh: 而故事也正是在这里变得有点复杂。

sentences.en: For a long time, there was no fixed script.
sentences.zh: 很长一段时间里，并没有固定的剧本。

sentences.en: Each professor performed his own version of the show, with his own characters, his own jokes, and his own running order.
sentences.zh: 每个“教授”都表演自己版本的节目，有他自己的角色、他自己的笑话和他的自己的一套出场顺序。

sentences.en: The most famous surviving version comes from the late 1820s, when a writer called John Payne Collier recorded, or claimed to record, the performance of a Punch performer named Giovanni Piccini.
sentences.zh: 现存最著名的版本可以追溯到 1820 年代后期，当时一位名叫 John Payne Collier 的作家记录（或者声称记录）了一位名叫 Giovanni Piccini 的 Punch 表演者的演出。

sentences.en: The book was illustrated by a celebrated caricaturist and it was given a wonderful title: "The Tragical Comedy or Comical Tragedy of Punch and Judy".
sentences.zh: 这本书由一位著名的漫画家配图，并有一个绝妙的书名：《Punch and Judy 的悲喜剧或滑稽悲剧》。

sentences.en: This 1828 book became the canonical version of the show.
sentences.zh: 这本 1828 年的书成为了该剧的正统版本。

sentences.en: It is what most people today think of as the "traditional" script.
sentences.zh: 它也是今天大多数人所认为的“传统”剧本。

sentences.en: There is, however, a slight problem with it.
sentences.zh: 然而，它存在一点小问题。

sentences.en: John Payne Collier was one of the most prolific literary forgers in English history.
sentences.zh: John Payne Collier 是英国历史上最多产的文学造假者之一。

sentences.en: He spent much of his later career inserting fake notes and fake documents into early Shakespeare editions, and getting caught doing so.
sentences.zh: 他的后半生很大一部分时间都在早期的莎士比亚版本中塞入虚假的笔记和虚假的文件，并因此被抓包。

sentences.en: So historians today are not entirely sure how much of what he wrote down in 1828 was a faithful record of what Piccini actually performed, and how much was tidied up, polished, or simply invented.
sentences.zh: 因此，今天的历史学家并不完全确定他在 1828 年写下的内容中，有多少是对 Piccini 实际表演的忠实记录，又有多少是被美化、润色或纯粹虚构出来的。

sentences.en: What is clear is the cast list, because most of these characters appear again and again in earlier descriptions.
sentences.zh: 清晰明确的是演员名单，因为这些角色在早期的描述中反复出现。

sentences.en: There is Punch himself. There is his wife Judy, hence the name, "Punch and Judy".
sentences.zh: 有 Punch 本人。有他的妻子 Judy，因此得名“Punch and Judy”。

sentences.en: There is their baby. There is Toby the dog, who in earlier shows was an actual live, performing dog who sat on the front of the booth.
sentences.zh: 有他们的婴儿。有小狗 Toby，在早期的演出中，这是一只真正的、会在布罩前表演的活狗。

sentences.en: There is the policeman. There is a clown called Joey.
sentences.zh: 有警察。有一个名叫 Joey 的小丑。

sentences.en: There is Jack Ketch, the hangman. There is a hungry crocodile, who is usually interested in Punch’s sausages, which Punch has for reasons that aren't entirely clear.
sentences.zh: 有刽子手 Jack Ketch。还有一条饥肠辘辘的鳄鱼，它通常对 Punch 的香肠感兴趣，而 Punch 带着香肠的原因并不是十分明了。

sentences.en: And in many versions, there is the devil himself, who arrives at the end to drag Mr Punch off to hell.
sentences.zh: 在许多版本中，甚至还有魔鬼本人，他在最后登场，把 Mr Punch 拖进地狱。

sentences.en: The plot, what actually happens in a Punch and Judy show, is famously violent.
sentences.zh: 剧情——也就是 Punch and Judy 演出中实际发生的事情——以暴力闻名。

sentences.en: A typical show goes something like this.
sentences.zh: 一个典型的演出大致是这样的。

sentences.en: Punch is left to look after the baby. The baby cries.
sentences.zh: Punch 被留下照顾婴儿。婴儿哭了。

sentences.en: Punch loses patience and throws it out of the window.
sentences.zh: Punch 失去耐心，把它扔出了窗外。

sentences.en: Judy returns, understandably furious. She attacks Punch, Punch attacks Judy, and before long she too has been knocked aside.
sentences.zh: Judy 回来了，理所当然地勃然大怒。她攻击 Punch，Punch 反击 Judy，没过多久她也被打倒在一旁。

sentences.en: Then society starts arriving to restore order.
sentences.zh: 接着社会开始介入以恢复秩序。

sentences.en: A policeman comes to arrest Punch. Punch beats the policeman.
sentences.zh: 一个警察来逮捕 Punch。Punch 把警察痛打一顿。

sentences.en: A hangman comes to execute Punch. Punch tricks the hangman into putting his own head in the noose.
sentences.zh: 一个刽子手来处决 Punch。Punch 诱骗刽子手把自己的头套进套索里。

sentences.en: A crocodile appears and tries to steal the sausages.
sentences.zh: 鳄鱼出现并试图偷走香肠。

sentences.en: Punch fights the crocodile. And in some versions, when even the devil comes to drag him down to hell, Punch beats the devil too, cackling while all of this is going on.
sentences.zh: Punch 与鳄鱼搏击。在某些版本中，甚至连魔鬼来把他拖入地狱时，Punch 也把魔鬼痛打了一顿，这一切发生时他还在咯咯傻笑。

sentences.en: After each successful act of violence, Punch leans forward and shouts his catchphrase to the audience through the swazzle: "That's the way to do it!"
sentences.zh: 在每一次成功的暴力行过后，Punch 都会前倾身体，通过 swazzle 向观众大喊他的口号：“That's the way to do it!（这就对了！）”

sentences.en: And the audience, at least most of the time, roars with laughter.
sentences.zh: 而观众，至少在大多数时候，都会爆发出大笑。

sentences.en: Now, by the early nineteenth century, Mr Punch was already a familiar street character in London and other large English cities.
sentences.zh: 到了十九世纪初，Mr Punch 已经是伦敦和其他英国大城市里人们熟知的街头角色了。

sentences.en: The booth could be set up on any corner, the show drew in a crowd, and the professor passed a hat at the end for tips.
sentences.zh: 布罩可以搭在任何街角，演出能吸引大批观众，而“教授”在演出结束时会传递帽子来收集小费。

sentences.en: It was rough, urban, working-class entertainment — no longer the preserve of Samuel Pepys and his beloved parmesan.
sentences.zh: 这是粗粝的、都市的、工人阶级的娱乐活动——不再是 Samuel Pepys 和他挚爱的帕玛森奶酪的专属。

sentences.en: Then came two big changes. The first was the railway.
sentences.zh: 随后迎来了两个巨大的改变。第一个是铁路。

sentences.en: From the 1840s onwards, the British railway network exploded.
sentences.zh: 从 1840 年代开始，英国铁路网迅猛发展。

sentences.en: For the first time, working people in industrial cities had cheap, fast access to the coast.
sentences.zh: 工业城市的劳动人民破天荒地得以低成本、快速地到达海岸线。

sentences.en: Small fishing villages turned into booming holiday resorts, as we'll be talking more about in part three.
sentences.zh: 正如我们将在第三部分中详细谈到的那样，小渔村变成了蓬勃发展的度假胜地。

sentences.en: And what did the new day-trippers want at the seaside, alongside sand and ice cream?
sentences.zh: 而除了沙滩和冰淇淋，新的日游游客在海滨想要什么呢？

sentences.en: They wanted entertainment. Punch professors were perfectly placed to provide it.
sentences.zh: 他们想要娱乐。Punch 教授们处于提供这种娱乐的绝佳位置。

sentences.en: The booth, with its tall stripes of red and white, was already portable.
sentences.zh: 那个有着醒目红白条纹的布罩本来就已经很便携了。

sentences.en: The show was already short, loud, and easy to follow.
sentences.zh: 演出本来就很短、很吵、而且很容易看懂。

sentences.en: All a professor had to do was pack up his cart, get on a train, and set up shop on the beach.
sentences.zh: 一个“教授”所要做的只是打包好他的手推车，坐上火车，然后在沙滩上开张。

sentences.en: By the late Victorian period, the red-and-white striped puppet booth had become one of the most recognisable images of the British seaside.
sentences.zh: 到了维多利亚时代晚期，红白相间的木偶布罩已经成为了英国海滨最具辨识度的标志之一。

sentences.en: The second big change was a magazine. In July 1841, two journalists in London started a new weekly satirical publication.
sentences.zh: 第二个巨大的改变是一本杂志。1841 年 7 月，伦敦的两位记者创办了一份新的每周讽刺刊物。

sentences.en: They needed a name, and they needed a mascot.
sentences.zh: 他们需要一个名字，也需要一个吉祥物。

sentences.en: They settled on the most famously anarchic, disrespectful, authority-mocking character they could think of, and they called their magazine "Punch", after Mr Punch himself.
sentences.zh: 他们最终敲定了他们能想到的最标新立异、最离经叛道、最喜欢嘲弄权威的角色，并以 Mr Punch 本人的名字将他们的杂志命名为《Punch》。

sentences.en: The full title was "Punch, or the London Charivari", and on its cover, week after week, Mr Punch and his dog Toby looked out at the reader.
sentences.zh: 全名是《Punch, or the London Charivari》，在其封面上，周复一周，Mr Punch 和他的狗 Toby 注视着读者。

sentences.en: The magazine started small. But by the 1850s it was selling forty thousand copies a week, and by 1910 over a hundred thousand.
sentences.zh: 这本杂志起步时规模很小。但到了 1850 年代，它的每周销量达到了四万册，而到 1910 年则超过了十万册。

sentences.en: For Victorian Britain, this gave Mr Punch a kind of double life.
sentences.zh: 对于维多利亚时代的英国来说，这赋予了 Mr Punch 一种双重生活。

sentences.en: On the beach, he was a cheap, knockabout puppet act for children.
sentences.zh: 在海滩上，他是给孩子们看的廉价、打闹的木偶戏。

sentences.en: In a smart London club, he was the cover star of the country's most prestigious satirical magazine.
sentences.zh: 在伦敦的高级俱乐部里，他是全国最具声望的讽刺杂志的封面明星。

sentences.en: The same hook-nosed troublemaker stood for both.
sentences.zh: 同一个鹰钩鼻的捣蛋鬼代表了这两者。

sentences.en: He had become a kind of national symbol of British misrule: the small voice that mocks authority, breaks the rules, and gets away with it.
sentences.zh: 他已经成为英国无政府状态的一种国家象征：那个嘲笑权威、打破规则却又能逍遥法外的微小声音。

sentences.en: But the world that had made Punch and Judy famous did not last.
sentences.zh: 然而，造就 Punch and Judy 辉煌的世界并没有持续下去。

sentences.en: In its heyday, there were an estimated 400 Punch men, or professors, in Britain.
sentences.zh: 在其鼎盛时期，英国估计有 400 名 Punch 艺人或“教授”。

sentences.en: In 1939, a survey counted only forty-four professional Punch men.
sentences.zh: 1939 年，一项调查仅统计到了 44 名专业的 Punch 艺人。

sentences.en: And by the end of the twentieth century, that number had fallen to around twelve.
sentences.zh: 而到了二十世纪末，这个数字已经降至 12 人左右。

sentences.en: There are some obvious reasons. From the 1960s onwards, cheap flights and package holidays meant that British holidaymakers increasingly jetted off for the south of Spain rather than sitting on a windy beach in northern England.
sentences.zh: 这其中有一些显而易见的原因。从 1960 年代起，廉价航班和包价旅游意味着英国度假者越来越多地坐飞机前往西班牙南部，而不是坐在英格兰北部风刮个不停的海滩上。

sentences.en: With fewer day-trippers, there was less work for Punch professors, and fewer young people willing to spend years learning the swazzle for a shrinking audience.
sentences.zh: 随着日游游客减少，Punch 教授们的工作也变少了，愿意花几年时间为日渐缩小的观众群体学习 swazzle 的年轻人也越来越少。

sentences.en: There is also the argument that the style of the show, what was happening on stage, was simply losing its appeal.
sentences.zh: 还有一个论点是，该节目的风格，也就是舞台上正在发生的事情，正在失去吸引力。

sentences.en: The most obvious problem is the violence against women.
sentences.zh: 最显而易见的问题是对女性的暴力。

sentences.en: It is a violent show with a violent male protagonist who beats his wife with a stick, throws his baby out of a window, and then cackles "That's the way to do it!".
sentences.zh: 这是一个暴力的节目，里面有一个暴力的男性主角，他用棍子殴打妻子，把婴儿扔出窗外，然后咯咯笑着说“这就对了！”。

sentences.en: To a lot of people, that was increasingly not funny, not something they wanted to watch.
sentences.zh: 对许多人来说，这越来越不好笑了，这不是他们想看的东西。

sentences.en: Domestic abuse charities have argued that the show makes light of violence in the home.
sentences.zh: 家庭虐待慈善机构认为，该节目将家庭暴力轻描淡写。

sentences.en: Women's rights campaigners have questioned what message it sends to small children.
sentences.zh: 女性权益活动人士质疑这向小孩子传递了什么样的信息。

sentences.en: And in some places, perfectly understandably, this argument has won.
sentences.zh: 在某些地方，这种争论完全可以理解地取得了胜利。

sentences.en: A town council in South Wales removed a Punch and Judy show from a local festival on the grounds that it was, in their words, "too violent and contained inappropriate hitting".
sentences.zh: 南威尔士的一个镇议会以该节目“过于暴力且包含不当击打”为由，将一场 Punch and Judy 演出从当地的节日中取消了。

sentences.en: And there was a recent survey of two thousand British parents that found around forty per cent thought the traditional Punch and Judy was too violent for their own children.
sentences.zh: 最近有一项针对两千名英国父母的调查发现，大约百分之四十的人认为传统的 Punch and Judy 对他们自己的孩子来说过于暴力了。

sentences.en: The defenders of the show have their own arguments.
sentences.zh: 节目的捍卫者们也有他们自己的论点。

sentences.en: They say it is satire, not instruction. They say Punch has always been a wicked character, and that the joke is on him, not on his victims.
sentences.zh: 他们说这是讽刺，而不是教导。他们说 Punch 一直是个邪恶的角色，笑话是在他身上，而不是在他的受害者身上。

sentences.en: They point out that he ends up in hell in many versions of the script, which is hardly an endorsement of his behaviour.
sentences.zh: 他们指出，在剧本的许多版本中，他最终都落入了地狱，这绝不是对他的行为的赞同。

sentences.en: They also argue that children do not read puppet violence in the same way adults do: the violence is stylised, ridiculous, and obviously unreal.
sentences.zh: 他们还认为，儿童对木偶暴力的解读与成年人不同：这种暴力是风格化的、荒谬的、显然是不真实的。

sentences.en: They suggest that this is nothing compared to many video games, where characters do much worse.
sentences.zh: 他们暗示，与许多角色干坏事得多的电子游戏相比，这根本不算什么。

sentences.en: And they argue that taking the violence out of Punch and Judy is a bit like taking the wolf out of Little Red Riding Hood.
sentences.zh: 他们认为，把 Punch and Judy 中的暴力成分去掉，有点像把《小红帽》里的大灰狼去掉。

sentences.en: You can do it, but at the end it's not really the same story.
sentences.zh: 你可以这么做，但到头话剧终究不再是同一个故事了。

sentences.en: This being said, there have been attempts to modernise, creating less violent versions of the show, or versions where Judy hits Punch as much as he hits her.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，也有人试图进行现代化改造，创作出暴力较少的版本，或者是 Judy 殴打 Punch 的次数和 Punch 打她一样多的版本。

sentences.en: The thing is, there really isn't a pure, original version.
sentences.zh: 问题是，根本没有一个纯粹的、最初的版本。

sentences.en: It has always changed. Punch looks different, what happens in the show has evolved, it has never been a single, fixed text.
sentences.zh: 它一直在改变。Punch 看起来不同，节目中发生的事情也在演变，它从来不是一个单一、固定的文本。

sentences.en: It is a tradition with a core set of characters, bent and rewritten in every generation that has performed it.
sentences.zh: 这是一个核心角色固定、但在每一个表演它的世代中都被扭曲和重写的传统。

sentences.en: So, what does the future hold for Punch and Judy??
sentences.zh: 那么，Punch and Judy 的未来会怎样呢？

sentences.en: Well, it is hard to imagine the show returning to the centre of British popular culture.
sentences.zh: 嗯，很难想象这个节目会重新回到英国大众文化的中心。

sentences.en: There are fewer professors than there used to be, and no great national movement to bring it back.
sentences.zh: 现在的“教授”比过去少了，也没有什么重大的全国性运动来复兴它。

sentences.en: If you are lucky, or unlucky, and you find yourself at a British seaside town, you might still stumble across the telltale red-and-white striped canopy of a Punch and Judy show, and hear the inimitable sound of the swazzle.
sentences.zh: 如果你足够幸运——或者说不幸——身处某个英国海滨小镇，你可能仍然会偶然遇到 Punch and Judy 那标志性的红白条纹遮阳棚，并听到 swazzle 那无与伦比的声音。

sentences.en: If you ever see one, stop for a moment and have a look at Mr Punch.
sentences.zh: 如果你有机会看到它，请停下一会儿，看一看 Mr Punch。

sentences.en: He has lasted three and a half centuries.
sentences.zh: 他已经持续了三个半世纪。

sentences.en: He has outlived the king who first applauded him in 1662.
sentences.zh: 他比 1962 年第一个为他鼓掌的国王活得还要久。

sentences.en: He has outlived the magazine that borrowed his name in 1841.
sentences.zh: 他比 1841 年借用他名字的杂志活得还要久。

sentences.en: He has outlived generations of children who once stood on the sand, staring up at that striped booth, laughing at a puppet who did everything he was not supposed to do.
sentences.zh: 他比一代又一代曾站在沙滩上、仰望那个条纹布罩、嘲笑一个做尽了不该做之事的木偶的孩子们活得还要久。

sentences.en: Whatever happens to him next, that is, by any standard, a pretty remarkable run.
sentences.zh: 无论他接下来遭遇什么，按任何标准来看，这都是一段相当了不起的历程。

sentences.en: OK, then, that is it for today's episode, the first part of our three-part mini-series on unusual British traditions.
sentences.zh: 好了，今天的节目就到这里，这是我们关于不寻常英国传统的三集迷你系列的第一部分。

sentences.en: Next up we'll be moving into fox hunting, a very different type of entertainment that many people would say is not entertainment at all.
sentences.zh: 接下来我们将进入猎狐环节，这是一种截然不同的娱乐活动，许多人会说这根本算不上娱乐。

sentences.en: And in part three, we'll tell the story of the rise and fall of the British seaside holiday, the place where Punch and Judy really became a cult tradition.
sentences.zh: 而在第三部分中，我们将讲述英国海滨度假的兴衰史，正是这个地方让 Punch and Judy 真正成了一种文化传统。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你收听的是由 Leonardo English 制作的《English Learning for Curious Minds》。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，大家注意安全，我们下期节目见。
